culture.title: Around the World: Making Wishes
points: In many countries, children make a wish when they blow out the candles on a birthday cake.
In Rome, visitors throw a coin into the Trevi Fountain and wish to return one day.
In some countries, people write their wishes for the new year in a notebook.
qs: Which of these traditions do you find the most interesting?
Do you think wishing is useful, or is it better to make a plan?

3-2.exit: Tell me two things you wish were different in your life right now, without help.

3-3.warmup: Where is the most beautiful place you have ever been?

expressions.def: far from the places tourists usually go
expressions.frame: I'd love to visit somewhere off the beaten track, like ___.

expressions.def: to start a journey
expressions.frame: On my dream trip, I'd set off from ___.

expressions.def: to visit famous places as a tourist
expressions.frame: If I were in ___, I'd go sightseeing at ___.

expressions.frame: Visiting ___ would be a dream come true.

dialogue.scene: Noura and Emma are looking at a travel magazine in the school library.

p1.t: Look at these photos! If you could go anywhere in the world, where would you go?
I'd go to Japan. Seeing Mount Fuji would be a dream come true.
Nice! What would you do there?
I'd go sightseeing in Kyoto, and I'd try real Japanese food. What about you?

p2.t: I'd go somewhere off the beaten track, like a small island in Indonesia.
How would you get there?
I'd set off from Jeddah and fly to Bali, then take a boat. The beaches would be stunning.
That sounds like a once-in-a-lifetime trip. I wish I could come with you!

dialogue.focus: Seeing Mount Fuji would be a dream come true.
qs: Why would Noura like to go to Japan?
How would Emma get to the island?

speakout.scene: You've won a competition, and the prize is a dream trip anywhere in the world! A travel agent is helping you plan it.

prompts.q: Congratulations! Where would you like to go?
prompts.hint: Use 'I'd love to go to …' and give a reason.

prompts.q: What would you do and see there?
prompts.hint: Use 'I'd …' twice, with two different activities.

prompts.q: Who would you take with you, and why?
prompts.hint: Use 'I'd take … because …'.

culture.title: Around Saudi Arabia: Dream Destinations at Home
points: The Red Sea coast has islands with coral reefs that divers dream of visiting.
In winter, the mountains of Abha and Al-Soudah are often covered in fog and look stunning.
The Empty Quarter is one of the largest sand deserts in the world.
qs: If a friend from abroad visited, which place would you take them to?
Would you rather explore the desert or the sea? Why?

3-3.exit: Tell me two sentences about your dream trip using 'would', without help.

3-4.objective: Today you will imagine difficult situations and say what you would do and why.
3-4.warmup: Have you ever had to make a difficult decision? What was it?

expressions.def: to act in an honest or good way
expressions.frame: If I ___, I'd do the right thing and ___.

expressions.def: to say what really happened
expressions.frame: I'd always tell the truth about ___.

expressions.def: to be unable to decide
expressions.frame: I'm in two minds about ___.

expressions.def: to say no to an offer
expressions.frame: I'd turn down ___ if ___.

expressions.def: to admit that you did something wrong
expressions.frame: If I broke something, I'd own up and ___.

expressions.def: a hard situation where you must choose
expressions.frame: A big dilemma for me would be ___.

dialogue.scene: Omar and Faisal are playing a 'What would you do?' card game during a long car journey to Abha.

p1.t: OK, next card. What would you do if you found 500 riyals in the street?
That's a real dilemma! I think I'd do the right thing and take it to the police station.
Really? I'm in two minds. If nobody saw me, I might keep it.
Come on! Imagine if it were your money.

p2.t: True. OK, your turn. What would you do if you broke your friend's tablet by accident?
I'd own up straight away and tell the truth. Then I'd offer to pay for it.
And if a famous team offered you a place, but you had to change schools?
Hmm, I'd probably turn it down. I wouldn't want to leave my friends.

dialogue.focus: I think I'd do the right thing and take it to the police station.
qs: What would Omar do with the money he found?
Why would Omar turn down the team's offer?

speakout.scene: You are a guest on a school radio show called 'What Would You Do?'. The presenter asks you about difficult situations.

prompts.q: What would you do if you saw a classmate cheating in an exam?
prompts.hint: Use 'If I saw …, I'd …' and give a reason.

prompts.q: What would you do if you broke something at a friend's house?
prompts.hint: Use 'I'd own up …' or 'I'd tell the truth …'.

prompts.q: Would you accept a great prize if it meant missing your best friend's big day?
prompts.hint: Say 'I'd accept it' or 'I'd turn it down' and explain why.

culture.title: Around the World: Honest Finds
points: In Japan, lost wallets are very often handed in to the police with all the money inside.
In Saudi Arabia, most malls and airports have a lost-and-found office.
A study in many countries found that people returned wallets more often when there was more money inside.
qs: Why do you think people return lost things?
What would you do if you lost something important?

3-4.exit: Tell me what you would do in one difficult situation and why, in two sentences, without help.

expressions.def: to have a good effect on people or a situation
expressions.frame: If everyone recycled, it would make a big difference to ___.

expressions.def: to remove something you don't want
expressions.frame: In my ideal city, we'd get rid of ___.

expressions.def: to use or do less of something
expressions.frame: If people cut down on ___, ___.

expressions.def: buses and trains that everyone can use
expressions.frame: If there were more public transport, ___.

dialogue.scene: Reem is preparing a two-minute talk called 'My Ideal City' for her English class. She practises with her mother.

p1.t: So, Reem, what would your ideal city be like?
In an ideal world, my city would have lots of green spaces. Every neighbourhood would have a park.
Lovely. What about traffic?
If there were more public transport, people wouldn't need to drive everywhere. The air would be cleaner.

p2.t: And what would you get rid of?
I'd get rid of plastic bags. If everyone cut down on plastic, it would make a huge difference.
Is there anything you wish for right now?
I wish more people cared about the environment. If only it were that easy!

dialogue.focus: If there were more public transport, people wouldn't need to drive everywhere.
qs: What would every neighbourhood have in Reem's ideal city?
What would Reem get rid of?

speakout.scene: Your school is holding a 'Design the Future' competition. Give a short talk about your ideal city. The judges ask you questions.

prompts.q: What would your ideal city be like?
prompts.hint: Describe two things with 'In my ideal city, there would be …'.

prompts.q: How would life be different for people there?
prompts.hint: Use 'If …, people would …' to show a result.

prompts.q: What do you wish were different in your city now?
prompts.hint: Use 'I wish …' or 'If only …' and finish with one strong idea.

culture.title: Around Saudi Arabia: Cities of the Future
points: The Green Riyadh project plans to plant millions of trees across the capital.
The Saudi Green Initiative aims to plant billions of trees across the country in the coming decades.
New tourist projects on the Red Sea coast are being designed to run on clean energy.
qs: Which of these projects do you think will make the biggest difference?
What small change could you make to help your city become greener?

3-5.exit: Describe your ideal world in two sentences, using 'would' and 'I wish', without help.

words.ex: My brother took up photography last year.
I got into chess after watching my uncle play.
In my spare time, I've been learning to cook.
Noura is keen on drawing and painting.
I've been making progress with my calligraphy.
Football has always been Omar's passion.

dialogue.t: Wow, Noura! Did you paint all of these?
Yes! I took up painting last summer, and I've been doing it every weekend since then.
They're amazing. How did you get into it?
My aunt is an artist. She showed me a few tricks, and I was hooked.
How long have you been painting this big one?
I've been working on it for three weeks. It shows the old houses in AlUla.
You've really made progress. Is painting your passion now?
Definitely. I spend most of my spare time on it. You're keen on drawing too, aren't you?

grammar.title: Present perfect continuous
grammar.ar: نستخدم have/has been + الفعل مع ing لنشاط بدأ في الماضي وما زال مستمراً. for للمدة، وsince لنقطة البداية.
examples: I've been painting for two years.
She has been playing padel since January.
How long have you been learning the guitar?

words.ex: Sam picked up some Arabic words from his neighbours.
I'm getting the hang of typing with ten fingers.
Don't give up. Practice makes perfect!
Omar struggled with the long words at first.
She has been improving step by step.
I feel more confident when I speak English now.

dialogue.t: Sam, your Arabic is really good now! How long have you been learning it?
I've been studying it since September. I have online lessons twice a week.
Is it difficult?
At first I struggled with the letters, but I'm getting the hang of them now.
And how have you been practising speaking?
I've been chatting with my neighbours. I've picked up lots of useful phrases from them.
That's great. You sound really confident.
Thanks! I'm making progress step by step. Practice makes perfect, as they say.

grammar.title: for vs since
grammar.ar: for + مدة زمنية (for two weeks)، وsince + نقطة بداية (since Monday / since 2024).
examples: I've been learning to swim for six months.
He's been studying Arabic since September.
We've been practising since the summer holiday.

words.ex: It took Emma a month to settle in at her new school.
We moved to Dammam in 2022.
Now I really feel at home in Riyadh.
Our neighbourhood has a big park.
I'm getting used to the hot weather.
Reem made friends quickly at her new school.

dialogue.t: Emma, how long have you been living in Riyadh?
We've been living here for eight months. We moved to Riyadh last spring.
Was it hard to settle in?
A little. I had to get used to the heat, and I missed my old friends.
And now? Have you made friends?
Yes, lots! I took up basketball, and I've been going to a club since October. Everyone there is lovely.
Do you like our neighbourhood?
I love it. There's a park and a great bakery. I really feel at home now.

grammar.title: How long …? + present perfect continuous
grammar.ar: نسأل How long have you been …? عن مدة نشاط مستمر حتى الآن. مع live وwork يصح أيضاً: I have lived here for …
examples: How long have you been living here?
I've been living here since 2021.
She's been going to this school for three years.

words.ex: My dad works out at the gym three times a week.
Faisal has been running to get in shape.
Always warm up before you run.
I was out of breath after the race.
The coach shouted, 'Keep going! You're nearly there!'
Swimming is great for building stamina.

dialogue.t: Faisal, you look exhausted! What have you been doing?
I've been running in the park. The school fun run is next Friday.
How long have you been training for it?
For about six weeks. At first I was out of breath after one kilometre!
And now?
I've made real progress. Now I can run four kilometres. I've been working out with Dad to build my stamina.
Do you warm up first?
Always. And when it gets hard, I just keep going. I really want to get in shape.

grammar.title: Present perfect continuous for visible results
grammar.ar: نستخدم هذا الزمن لنشرح نتيجة نراها الآن: You look tired. — I've been running.
examples: Your face is red. Have you been running?
I'm tired because I've been training all morning.
He hasn't been sleeping well before the match.

words.ex: We've been working on a robot for the science fair.
So far, we've built the base of the model.
Reem came up with a brilliant name for the team.
The project is a bit behind schedule.
The deadline for the report is next Thursday.
I teamed up with two classmates for the competition.

dialogue.t: Hello, girls. How's your science project going?
Quite well, thanks. We've been working on a solar oven for two weeks.
Great idea! Who came up with it?
Reem did. Then she teamed up with me because I'm good at building things.
What have you done so far?
So far we've built the box, and we've been testing it on the roof every afternoon.
The deadline is next Thursday. Are you behind schedule?
A little, but we've been staying after school, and we're catching up step by step.

grammar.title: Present perfect continuous vs present perfect simple
grammar.ar: المستمر (I've been building) يركّز على النشاط ومدّته؛ البسيط (I've built) يركّز على النتيجة المنجزة.
examples: We've been building the model for a week.
We've built the base, but not the roof.
She's been writing the report all morning, and she's written five pages.

words.ex: Last year, Faisal took up karate.
She has made great progress in maths.
She gained experience by helping at her uncle's shop.
I'm proud of finishing the fun run.
Teamwork is one of my strengths.
I'm looking forward to meeting new people.

dialogue.t: Thanks for joining us, Noura. Tell me about something you've been doing outside school.
I've been volunteering at a children's library since last January. I read stories to young kids.
What experience have you gained there?
I've learnt to be patient, and I've become a much more confident speaker.
Have you taken up anything else recently?
Yes, I've been learning to code for about six months. I've made a lot of progress.
Wonderful. What are you most proud of?
I've built a small quiz app for my class. I'm really looking forward to learning more this summer.

grammar.title: Talking about experiences in detail
grammar.ar: نجمع: المضارع التام المستمر للنشاط المستمر (I've been coding) + المضارع التام للإنجاز (I've built an app) + الماضي البسيط لوقت محدد (I started in May).
examples: I've been coding for six months.
I've built two small apps so far.
I started in May, after my exams.

words.ex: Al-Qassim is famous for its dates.
Saudi coffee is made from lightly roasted beans.
Saudi Arabia exports dates to many countries.
The date harvest is in late summer.
Some carpets are still made by hand.
Taif rose oil is very high quality.

dialogue.t: There are so many dates here! Where do they all come from?
Most of them are grown here in Al-Qassim. Our region is famous for its dates.
When are they picked?
The harvest is in late summer. Some farmers still pick the best dates by hand.
Are they only sold in Saudi Arabia?
No, they're exported to many countries around the world.
And what's this sweet brown paste?
It's made from dates. It's used in lots of desserts, and it's very high quality.

grammar.title: Present passive: is / are + past participle
grammar.ar: نستخدم المبني للمجهول عندما يهمّنا الشيء أكثر من الفاعل: Dates are grown in Al-Qassim.
examples: Dates are grown in Al-Qassim.
Rose oil is made from petals.
These carpets are made by hand.

words.ex: Masmak Fortress dates back to the 1860s.
The old market is a popular tourist attraction.
The museum was designed by a famous architect.
Concerts take place there every winter.
The old palace was restored a few years ago.
Kingdom Centre is a famous Riyadh landmark.

dialogue.t: This fort looks really old. When was it built?
Masmak Fortress dates back to the 1860s. It was built from mud bricks.
Wow! Has it always looked this good?
No, it was restored, and now it's a museum. Festivals sometimes take place in the square outside.
It's a great tourist attraction. What's that tall building with the hole at the top?
That's Kingdom Centre, another famous landmark. It was designed by an international team.
When was it opened?
It was opened in 2002. It's famous for its sky bridge, which is visited by lots of tourists.

grammar.title: Past passive: was / were + past participle
grammar.ar: نستخدم was/were + التصريف الثالث لأحداث الماضي، ونذكر الفاعل بعد by إذا كان مهماً.
examples: Masmak Fortress was built in the 1860s.
Kingdom Centre was designed by an international team.
The old houses were restored last year.

words.ex: A compass is used for finding directions.
The internet changed the world.
Some great discoveries were made by accident.
Al-Jazari was a brilliant inventor.
Mobile phones came into use in the 1980s.
He figured out how to move water with machines.

dialogue.t: What's this strange machine with the elephant?
It's a copy of the Elephant Clock. It was designed by Al-Jazari more than 800 years ago.
Who was he?
He was a brilliant inventor and engineer. He figured out how to move water with machines.
What was the clock used for?
It was used for telling the time. Every half hour, a little figure moved and a sound was made.
Was it invented by accident?
Not at all! It was carefully planned. Some of his ideas came into use much later and helped change the world.

grammar.title: Passive with by + agent
grammar.ar: نضيف by + الفاعل عندما نريد أن نذكر من قام بالفعل: It was invented by …
examples: The telephone was invented by Alexander Graham Bell.
The clock was designed by Al-Jazari.
Penicillin was discovered partly by accident.

words.ex: Mr Saad is in charge of the sports teams.
Please hand in your projects on Sunday.
We aren't allowed to use phones in class.
Science is on my timetable twice a week.
The canteen is supervised by two teachers.
The winners were announced at morning assembly.

dialogue.t: Omar, what happens in the morning? Is there an assembly?
Yes. Morning assembly is held at seven. Important news is announced there.
And when is lunch served?
It's served at half past eleven. The canteen is supervised by Mr Saad.
How is homework given?
It's posted on the school app, and it has to be handed in by Thursday.
Are we allowed to use phones?
Only at break. Mr Saad is in charge of that too, so be careful! Your timetable is on the app as well.

grammar.title: Present passive for routines and rules
grammar.ar: نستخدم المبني للمجهول لوصف الأنظمة والإجراءات: Lunch is served at 11:30. Phones aren't allowed.
examples: Lunch is served at half past eleven.
Homework is posted on the app.
Phones aren't allowed in class.

words.ex: The match was called off because of the storm.
The trip was put off until next week.
According to the news, the road was closed.
Heavy rain fell in Jeddah last night.
Sixty thousand spectators watched the final.
The winners were announced on TV.

dialogue.t: Did you hear? Tomorrow's school trip was called off.
Really? Why?
According to the school website, heavy rain is expected in Riyadh tomorrow.
That's a pity. Was it cancelled completely or just put off?
It was put off until next Tuesday. It was announced this morning.
OK. And what happened in the football final last night?
Our team won 2–1! The winning goal was scored in the last minute.
Amazing. I heard more than 60,000 spectators were there.

grammar.title: Past passive in news reports
grammar.ar: في الأخبار نستخدم المبني للمجهول لأن الحدث أهم من الفاعل: The match was called off.
examples: The match was called off because of the storm.
The winners were announced on Monday.
Ten thousand tickets were sold in one hour.

words.ex: AlUla is located in the north-west of Saudi Arabia.
The tombs date back about 2,000 years.
The tombs were carved into the rocks.
Hegra was Saudi Arabia's first World Heritage Site.
AlUla is famous for its huge rocks.
The sunset over the rocks was breathtaking.

dialogue.t: OK, Reem, start your fact file. Where is AlUla?
AlUla is located in the north-west of Saudi Arabia. It's famous for its huge rocks and ancient tombs.
How old are the tombs?
The tombs at Hegra date back about 2,000 years. They were carved into the rocks by the Nabataeans.
Is the area protected?
Yes. In 2008, Hegra was listed as Saudi Arabia's first World Heritage Site.
Do many people go there now?
It's visited by thousands of tourists every year. The views are breathtaking, especially at sunset.

grammar.title: Present and past passive together
grammar.ar: في عرض الحقائق نخلط: is/are + pp للحاضر (It's visited by …) وwas/were + pp للماضي (It was carved …).
examples: AlUla is visited by thousands of tourists.
The tombs were carved about 2,000 years ago.
Hegra was listed as a World Heritage Site in 2008.

words.ex: I'm afraid this soup is cold.
Could you possibly bring me some water?
I think there's been a mix-up with our drinks.
He sent the burger back because it was cold.
The chicken was undercooked, so we sent it back.
The waiter gave us free dessert to make up for the wait.

dialogue.t: Excuse me. I'm afraid there's a problem with my order.
Oh, I'm sorry. What's wrong?
I ordered grilled chicken, but this is fried fish. I think there's been a mix-up.
I do apologise. I'll send it back to the kitchen right away.
Thank you. Could you possibly check the chicken isn't undercooked? Last time it was a bit pink inside.
Of course. Would you like anything while you wait?
I'd like some more water, please.
Certainly. And to make up for the wait, your dessert is free tonight.

grammar.title: Polite complaints: I'm afraid … / Could you possibly …?
grammar.ar: نبدأ الشكوى بـ I'm afraid … لتلطيفها، ونطلب الحل بـ Could you possibly + الفعل؟
examples: I'm afraid this soup is cold.
Could you possibly bring me another one?
I'd like to change my order, please.

words.ex: Unfortunately, the box was damaged.
I asked for a refund because the shoes were too small.
They sent me a replacement charger the next day.
Would it be possible to change the colour?
The parcel turned up three days late.
Sorry, the blue one is out of stock.

dialogue.t: Good afternoon, customer service. How can I help you?
Hello. I'm calling about my order. Unfortunately, the headphones turned up yesterday with a broken cable.
I'm sorry to hear that. Could you give me your order number, please?
Yes, it's 45821. I'd like a replacement, please.
Let me check. I'm afraid that model is out of stock at the moment.
Oh no. Would it be possible to get a different colour instead?
Yes, we have them in white. Or I can give you a full refund.
I'd rather have the white ones, thanks. When will they arrive?

grammar.title: Polite requests: Would it be possible to …?
grammar.ar: Would it be possible to + الفعل؟ أكثر تهذيباً من Can you …؟ ونستخدم I'd like … لنقول ما نريده.
examples: Would it be possible to change the size?
I'd like a full refund, please.
Unfortunately, the box was damaged.

words.ex: Sorry to bother you, but the lift isn't working.
The air conditioner broke down last night.
They fixed the shower in ten minutes.
The manager promised to look into it.
Please send someone as soon as possible.
The room next to the lift is very noisy.

dialogue.t: Good evening. Sorry to bother you, but there's a problem in room 214.
Good evening. What seems to be the problem?
I'm afraid the air conditioner has broken down. It's really hot in the room.
I'm very sorry. I'll send someone to fix it as soon as possible.
Thank you. Also, the room is quite noisy. It's right next to the lift.
I see. I'll look into it. Would you like to move to a quieter room?
Yes, please. Could you possibly give us a room with a sea view?
Certainly. Room 509 is free. I'll ask someone to help with your bags.

grammar.title: Describing the problem
grammar.ar: نصف المشكلة بـ isn't working أو has broken down أو is too + صفة، ثم نطلب الحل بأدب.
examples: The shower isn't working.
I'm afraid the air conditioner has broken down.
The room is a bit too noisy.

words.ex: My father made a complaint about the parking.
I made a booking for the padel court at six.
We were turned away because the court was full.
It's not the first time the pool has been closed.

words.w: I'd appreciate it if you could …
words.ex: I'd appreciate it if you could call me back.
The manager sorted out the problem quickly.

dialogue.t: Good evening. I'd like to make a complaint, please.
Of course. What happened?
I made a booking for court 3 at six o'clock, but we were turned away. Someone else was playing.
Oh dear, I'm so sorry. Let me check the system.
It's not the first time, either. We had the same problem last week.
You're right. There's been a problem with our app, and we're sorting it out.
I'd appreciate it if you could give us another court tonight.
Of course. Court 5 is free now, and your next booking is free of charge.

grammar.title: More polite structures
grammar.ar: I'd like to make a complaint about … لبدء شكوى رسمية، وI'd appreciate it if you could + الفعل لطلب الحل بأدب شديد.
examples: I'd like to make a complaint about my booking.
I'd appreciate it if you could call me back.
It's not the first time this has happened.

words.ex: My tablet keeps switching off when I play games.
The phone is still under warranty, so the repair is free.
I dropped my phone, and now the screen is cracked.
My phone battery runs out by lunchtime.
They charged me 100 riyals for a new screen.
I'll get back to you tomorrow with the price.

dialogue.t: Hi there. What can I do for you?
Hi. I'm afraid my tablet keeps switching off, and the battery runs out after an hour.
I see. And the screen's cracked too. When did you buy it?
Last March, so it should still be under warranty.
Let me check. Yes, it is. We can fix the battery for free, but it'll take three days.
Three days? Could you possibly do it a bit faster? I need it for school.
I'll try my best. The screen isn't covered, though. We charge 200 riyals for that.
OK. Could you get back to me when it's ready?

grammar.title: keep + -ing for annoying repeated problems
grammar.ar: نستخدم keep + الفعل مع ing لمشكلة تتكرّر وتزعجنا: It keeps switching off.
examples: My laptop keeps freezing.
The printer keeps making a strange noise.
My phone keeps losing the Wi-Fi signal.

words.ex: I'm afraid my bag hasn't arrived.
Could you possibly deliver it by tomorrow?
My suitcase went missing at the airport.
Please keep me updated by text message.
The airline paid compensation for the delay.
So, just to confirm, you'll deliver it tomorrow?

dialogue.t: Lost baggage desk, Sarah speaking. How can I help?
Hello. I'm calling about my suitcase. I'm afraid it went missing on our flight from Riyadh this morning.
I'm sorry to hear that. Can you describe it?
It's a large blue suitcase with a red tag. All my clothes are in it.
Don't worry, we'll sort it out. We think it was put on the wrong plane, so it should arrive tomorrow.
Could you possibly deliver it to our hotel? And could you keep me updated?
